Arthur Conan Doyle, Brigadier Gerard Stories.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/arthur-conan-doyle/brigadier-gerard-stories

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Arthur Conan Doyle, the author, died 1930 (Wikidata Q35610, P570 = 1930-07-07).

First publication of the text used: between 1894 and 1910 (SE colophon: 'Brigadier Gerard Stories was compiled from short stories published between 1894 and 1910 by Arthur Conan Doyle.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in between 1894 and 1910, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each of these has a term of life + 70 years or less. The United States is also possible, and the text was first published before 1931, so the United States rule settles that case (see above). The last person named above, Arthur Conan Doyle, died in 1930, so the text entered the public domain in each of the other possible countries on 1 January 2001.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
